newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Jurong Shipyard to detail merger by May.
newsitem.headline: Jurong Shipyard to detail merger by May.

text.p: Jurong Shipyard Ltd's discussions on Sembawang Corp's (SembCorp) proposed merger plans are close to conclusion and details will be released by May, chairman Lua Cheng Eng said on Saturday.
"We are still in discussions on the proposed merger. We are coming almost to the conclusion of the discussions," Lua told Reuters.
Lua said he hoped details of the merger would be known in the next few weeks or before the group's annual general meeting in May.
"End May is the worst case scenario," Lua said after the company announced 1996 results which showed an 18 percent fall in net profits to Singapore $31.72 million on a turnover of S$357.2 million.
In November, SembCorp proposed a takeover if Jurong Shipyard in what amounted to a major shake up in Singapore's ship repair industry.

The deal, which had been expected to be completed early this year, would create the world's largest single ship repair group. In the proposed merger, SembCorp is to inject S$279.28 million worth of its shipyard and engineering assets into Jurong in return for some 41.07 million new Jurong shares.
This will raise SembCorp's stake in Jurong to 41.6 percent from 20 percent. Under Singapore's takeover and merger code, SembCorp must then make a general offer for all Jurong shares.
The new Jurong shares are valued at S$6.80 each.
"The proposal requires time. Many issues cannot be resolved that easily," Lua said, declining to detail these issues.
On Friday, Jurong shares ended unchanged at S$6.40 on 292,000 shares.
